topics: The Human Eye and the Colourful World

questions.q: Burning of magnesium ribbon in air to form magnesium oxide is an example of which type of reaction?
questions.explanation: Magnesium and oxygen combine to form a single product, so it is a combination reaction.

questions.q: When an iron nail is dipped in copper sulphate solution, the blue colour of the solution slowly fades. This happens because
options: iron is less reactive than copper
iron reacts with the water in the solution
iron displaces copper and forms pale green iron sulphate
questions.explanation: Iron is more reactive than copper, so it displaces copper: Fe + CuSO4 gives FeSO4 + Cu.

questions.q: In the reaction Fe2O3 + 2Al gives Al2O3 + 2Fe, used to join railway tracks, which substance is oxidised?
questions.explanation: Aluminium gains oxygen to form aluminium oxide, so it is oxidised, while iron(III) oxide loses oxygen and is reduced.

questions.q: Quicklime reacts vigorously with water to form
questions.explanation: CaO + H2O gives Ca(OH)2, slaked lime, releasing a lot of heat.

questions.q: Sodium sulphate solution is mixed with barium chloride solution and a white precipitate forms. The reaction is a
questions.explanation: The two compounds exchange ions to give BaSO4 (white precipitate) and NaCl, which is double displacement.

questions.q: Silver chloride kept in a white dish in sunlight turns grey. This is because
options: light decomposes it into silver and chlorine
it reacts with oxygen to form silver oxide
it absorbs moisture from the air
it melts in the heat of the Sun
questions.explanation: Sunlight causes a photochemical decomposition, 2AgCl giving 2Ag + Cl2, and the grey colour is silver metal.

questions.q: What is a balanced chemical equation and why must a chemical equation be balanced?
questions.answer: A balanced chemical equation has the same number of atoms of each element on both sides. It is needed because, by the law of conservation of mass, mass is neither created nor destroyed in a chemical reaction.
keyPoints: Equal number of atoms of each element on both sides
questions.explanation: Balancing makes the equation obey conservation of mass.

questions.q: Distinguish between exothermic and endothermic reactions, giving one example of each.
questions.answer: In an exothermic reaction heat is released, for example burning of natural gas or respiration. In an endothermic reaction heat is absorbed, for example decomposition of calcium carbonate on heating.
questions.explanation: The difference lies in whether the reaction gives out or takes in heat.

questions.q: Which of the following is a strong acid?
questions.explanation: Hydrochloric acid ionises almost completely in water, while the others are weak organic acids.

questions.q: A solution turns red litmus paper blue. The solution is most likely
questions.explanation: Bases turn red litmus blue.

questions.q: The soil in a farmer's field is too acidic for the crop. Which substance is most suitable to add to it?
questions.explanation: A base such as quicklime or slaked lime neutralises the excess acid in the soil.

questions.q: The chemical name of baking soda is
questions.explanation: Baking soda is NaHCO3, sodium hydrogencarbonate.

questions.q: Plaster of Paris is prepared by heating which substance at 373 K?
questions.explanation: Heating gypsum (CaSO4.2H2O) at 373 K gives plaster of Paris (CaSO4.1/2 H2O).

questions.q: Dry HCl gas does not change the colour of dry blue litmus paper, but moist blue litmus turns red. Why?
options: HCl produces H+ ions only in the presence of water
Dry litmus paper is damaged by the gas
HCl behaves as a base when it is dry
Water acts as a catalyst for litmus
questions.explanation: Acidic behaviour is due to H+ ions, which are released only when HCl dissolves in water.

questions.q: What is the pH scale? What is the pH of a neutral solution?
questions.answer: The pH scale is a scale from 0 to 14 that measures how acidic or basic a solution is. A neutral solution such as pure water has pH 7; below 7 is acidic and above 7 is basic.
questions.explanation: pH indicates hydrogen ion concentration on a convenient scale.

questions.q: Why does taking an antacid tablet give relief from acidity in the stomach?
questions.answer: Acidity is caused by excess hydrochloric acid in the stomach. An antacid contains a mild base such as magnesium hydroxide, which neutralises the extra acid.
keyPoints: Excess HCl in stomach causes acidity
questions.explanation: A base neutralises the acid, relieving the discomfort.

questions.q: Which metal is liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Mercury is the only common metal that is liquid at room temperature.

questions.q: Which of these metals reacts most vigorously with cold water?
questions.explanation: Sodium is highly reactive and reacts violently with cold water, releasing hydrogen.

questions.q: Sodium and potassium are stored under kerosene oil because
options: they react very vigorously with oxygen and moisture in air
they are insoluble in kerosene only
they are too heavy to keep in air
questions.explanation: They are so reactive that they could catch fire in air, so kerosene keeps them away from oxygen and moisture.

questions.q: Brass is an alloy of
questions.explanation: Brass is made from copper and zinc.

questions.q: The property of metals by which they can be drawn into thin wires is called
questions.explanation: Ductility is the ability to be drawn into wires; malleability is being beaten into sheets.

questions.q: A gold ornament found in an ancient ruin is still shiny, but iron tools found with it are badly rusted. The best reason is that
options: gold is a better conductor than iron
gold is very unreactive and does not corrode easily
questions.explanation: Gold is low in the reactivity series, so it does not react with air or moisture.

questions.q: Define ore and gangue.
questions.answer: An ore is a mineral from which a metal can be extracted profitably. Gangue is the earthy impurities such as sand and soil present in the ore.
keyPoints: Ore is a mineral that yields metal profitably
Gangue is the impurities in the ore
questions.explanation: Gangue must be removed before extracting the metal.

questions.q: Aluminium is a reactive metal, yet aluminium utensils last long. Explain.
questions.answer: Aluminium forms a thin, tough layer of aluminium oxide on its surface when exposed to air. This layer is unreactive and protects the metal beneath from further corrosion.
keyPoints: A thin oxide layer forms on the surface
questions.explanation: The protective oxide film stops further corrosion.

questions.q: The valency of carbon is
questions.explanation: Carbon has four electrons in its outer shell and forms four covalent bonds.

questions.q: Which of the following is an unsaturated hydrocarbon?
questions.explanation: C2H4 (ethene) has a carbon-carbon double bond, so it is unsaturated.

questions.q: Soap helps remove oily dirt from clothes because
options: soap converts the oil to a gas
soap reacts with dirt to form an insoluble salt
soap dissolves the dirt like a solvent
soap molecules form micelles with the oil trapped inside
questions.explanation: The hydrocarbon tails of soap dissolve in oil while the ionic heads face water, forming micelles that are rinsed away.

questions.q: The functional group present in alcohols is
questions.explanation: Alcohols contain the hydroxyl group, -OH.

questions.q: When ethanoic acid reacts with sodium carbonate, the gas evolved is
questions.explanation: Acids react with carbonates to release carbon dioxide.

questions.q: Why do unsaturated hydrocarbons usually burn with a sooty yellow flame while saturated ones burn with a clean blue flame?
options: Unsaturated ones have a higher proportion of carbon that burns incompletely, giving soot
questions.explanation: A higher carbon percentage leads to incomplete combustion and soot in unsaturated compounds.

questions.q: Name the first four members of the alkane series and write their formulae.
questions.answer: Methane CH4, ethane C2H6, propane C3H8 and butane C4H10.
questions.explanation: Alkanes follow the general formula CnH(2n+2).

questions.q: What is a homologous series? Mention two features of it.
questions.answer: A homologous series is a family of organic compounds with the same functional group in which successive members differ by a CH2 unit. Members have similar chemical properties and show a gradual change in physical properties.
keyPoints: Similar chemical properties and gradation in physical properties
questions.explanation: Homologous series organise the study of carbon compounds.

questions.q: Photosynthesis takes place in which part of a plant cell?
questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll, which traps light energy.

questions.q: The enzyme in saliva that begins the digestion of starch is
questions.explanation: Salivary amylase breaks starch down into sugar in the mouth.

questions.q: In a plant that has gone without water for many days the stomata close. This is because the guard cells
options: lose water and shrink, closing the pore
questions.explanation: Guard cells open the pore when they take in water and close it when they lose water, reducing water loss.

questions.q: The basic filtering unit of the kidney is the
questions.explanation: Each kidney has many nephrons that filter blood to form urine.

questions.q: The blood vessel that carries oxygenated blood from the lungs to the heart is the
questions.explanation: The pulmonary vein returns oxygen-rich blood to the left atrium.

questions.q: Arteries have thicker, more elastic walls than veins because
options: arteries contain valves to stop backflow
blood leaves the heart through them under high pressure
arteries only carry blood to the lungs
questions.explanation: Blood pumped out of the heart is under high pressure, so artery walls must withstand it.

questions.q: Write the process of photosynthesis in words and mention the conditions needed.
questions.answer: Carbon dioxide and water, in the presence of sunlight and chlorophyll, are converted into glucose (carbohydrate) and oxygen is released.
keyPoints: Carbon dioxide and water are raw materials
questions.explanation: Photosynthesis is how green plants make their food.

questions.q: Why is the small intestine long and covered with villi?
questions.answer: The length gives enough time for complete digestion and absorption. Villi are finger-like projections that increase the surface area for absorbing digested food and are richly supplied with blood vessels.
keyPoints: Length allows complete digestion and absorption
questions.explanation: The structure suits absorption of food.

questions.q: Which part of a neuron receives information from other cells?
questions.explanation: Dendrites receive the signal and pass it to the cell body.

questions.q: A reflex action such as pulling the hand away from a hot object is mainly controlled by the
questions.explanation: Reflex arcs are processed in the spinal cord, which saves time.

questions.q: After a heavy meal rich in sugar, blood glucose rises. The body responds mainly by
options: secreting adrenaline from the adrenal glands
secreting growth hormone from the pituitary
questions.explanation: Insulin from the pancreas lowers blood sugar level.

questions.q: Which plant hormone is mainly responsible for the bending of a shoot towards light?
questions.explanation: Auxin collects on the shaded side and makes cells there grow longer, bending the shoot toward light.

questions.q: Iodine is needed in the diet to make which hormone?
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland to make thyroxine; lack of it causes goitre.

questions.q: A seedling is placed horizontally. After a few days its root bends downward and shoot bends upward. This shows
options: geotropism, with root positive and shoot negative
questions.explanation: Roots grow towards gravity (positive geotropism) and shoots away from it (negative geotropism).

questions.q: Name the three main parts of the human brain.
questions.answer: The forebrain (including the cerebrum), the midbrain and the hindbrain (cerebellum, pons and medulla).
questions.explanation: These are the three main regions of the brain.

questions.q: What is a reflex action? Give one example.
questions.answer: A reflex action is a sudden, automatic response to a stimulus that does not need thinking. For example, quickly withdrawing your hand on touching a hot object.
keyPoints: Quick automatic response to a stimulus
questions.explanation: Reflex actions protect the body quickly.

questions.q: Which of the following reproduces by budding?
questions.explanation: Hydra grows buds on its body that detach as new individuals.

questions.q: Binary fission in Amoeba produces
questions.explanation: The cell splits into two daughter Amoebae.

questions.q: Plants grown by vegetative propagation are very similar to the parent plant because
options: only one parent is involved and no gametes fuse
questions.explanation: Without fusion of gametes, there is little variation from the parent.

questions.q: The male reproductive part of a flower is the
questions.explanation: The stamen has an anther that produces pollen.

questions.q: In human females fertilisation normally takes place in the
questions.explanation: The sperm meets the egg in the oviduct (fallopian tube).

questions.q: Why is the placenta important during pregnancy?
options: It passes nutrients and oxygen from the mother to the embryo and removes its wastes
It stores eggs for later use
It protects the uterus from infection only
questions.explanation: The placenta has villi that exchange materials between mother and embryo.

questions.q: What is pollination? Name two agents of pollination.
questions.answer: Pollination is the transfer of pollen from the anther to the stigma of a flower. It is carried out by agents such as wind, insects, water or birds.
keyPoints: Transfer of pollen from anther to stigma
Two agents such as wind and insects
questions.explanation: Pollination must happen before fertilisation.

questions.q: Mention two methods by which unwanted pregnancy can be prevented.
questions.answer: Barrier methods such as a condom, oral contraceptive pills, a copper-T (intrauterine device), or surgical methods such as vasectomy and tubectomy.
keyPoints: Barrier method such as a condom
Another method such as pills, IUD or surgery
questions.explanation: Contraceptive methods prevent fertilisation or implantation.

questions.q: Who is known as the father of genetics?
questions.explanation: Mendel's experiments on garden pea established the basic rules of inheritance.

questions.q: A pure tall pea plant (TT) is crossed with a pure dwarf plant (tt). All plants of the F1 generation are
questions.explanation: All F1 plants are Tt, and tallness is dominant.

questions.q: A couple already has three daughters. What is the chance that their fourth child will be a girl?
questions.explanation: Each child has an independent 50% chance of being a girl, because the sperm carries X or Y with equal probability.

questions.q: How many pairs of chromosomes are present in a human body cell?
questions.explanation: A human cell has 46 chromosomes, which is 23 pairs.

questions.q: The phenotypic ratio in the F2 generation of a monohybrid cross is
questions.explanation: Three plants show the dominant trait for every one showing the recessive trait.

questions.q: In a dihybrid cross Mendel obtained a 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 ratio in F2. This shows that
options: the two traits always travel together
both traits are controlled by the same gene
the two traits are inherited independently of each other
questions.explanation: New combinations of traits appear, so the traits assort independently.

questions.q: What are dominant and recessive traits?
questions.answer: A dominant trait is the one that appears in the F1 generation when two contrasting traits are crossed. A recessive trait is the one that is hidden in F1 and reappears in F2.
keyPoints: Recessive trait is hidden in F1 and appears in F2
questions.explanation: This is the result of Mendel's monohybrid cross.

questions.q: Why are variations important for a species?
questions.answer: Variations help some individuals survive when the environment changes, such as in temperature or food supply. These individuals reproduce and pass on useful traits, so the species is not wiped out.
questions.explanation: Variation gives species a better chance of survival.

questions.q: Which type of mirror is used as a rear-view mirror in vehicles?
questions.explanation: A convex mirror gives an erect image and a wide field of view.

questions.q: The radius of curvature of a spherical mirror is 24 cm. Its focal length is
questions.explanation: Focal length is half the radius of curvature, f = R/2 = 12 cm.

questions.q: An object is placed at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror. The image formed is
options: real, inverted and the same size, at the centre of curvature
real, inverted and magnified, beyond the centre of curvature
real, inverted and diminished, between F and C
questions.explanation: When the object is at C, the image is at C, real, inverted and equal in size.

questions.q: The SI unit of power of a lens is
questions.explanation: Power is 1/f with f in metres, and its unit is the dioptre.

questions.q: The refractive index of a medium is equal to
options: speed of light in the medium divided by speed in vacuum
speed of light in the medium multiplied by speed in vacuum
speed of light in vacuum multiplied by the wavelength
speed of light in vacuum divided by speed in the medium
questions.explanation: n = c/v, the ratio of the speed in vacuum to the speed in the medium.

questions.q: A concave lens has a focal length of 25 cm. Its power is
questions.explanation: P = 1/f = 1/(-0.25 m) = -4 D, negative for a concave lens.

questions.q: State the two laws of reflection of light.
questions.answer: The angle of incidence is equal to the angle of reflection. The incident ray, the reflected ray and the normal at the point of incidence all lie in the same plane.
keyPoints: Angle of incidence equals angle of reflection
Incident ray, reflected ray and normal in the same plane
questions.explanation: These laws apply to all reflecting surfaces.

questions.q: State two uses of concave mirrors.
questions.answer: They are used in torches and vehicle headlights to send out parallel beams, as shaving mirrors to see a magnified face, by dentists to see enlarged images of teeth, and in solar furnaces.
questions.explanation: A concave mirror can converge light or give a magnified erect image at close range.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: Which part of the eye controls the size of the pupil?
questions.explanation: The iris is a muscular diaphragm that changes pupil size to regulate light entering the eye.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: Myopia (short-sightedness) is corrected using
questions.explanation: A concave lens diverges the rays so that the image falls on the retina.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: In a myopic eye, the image of a distant object is formed
questions.explanation: The eyeball is too long or the lens too converging, so the focus is in front of the retina.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The splitting of white light into its component colours is called
questions.explanation: Dispersion happens because different colours bend by different amounts in a prism.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The sky appears blue mainly because
options: it reflects the colour of the sea
air molecules scatter shorter wavelengths more strongly
questions.explanation: Blue light has a shorter wavelength and is scattered more by the very small particles in air.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: The Sun appears red at sunrise and sunset because
options: its light travels a longer path in the atmosphere, so blue is scattered away and red reaches us
the Sun becomes cooler at those times
the atmosphere absorbs all blue light
the Sun is closer to the Earth
questions.explanation: On the long path through air, most blue light is scattered out of the beam, leaving red.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: What is meant by the power of accommodation of the eye? What is the near point of a normal eye?
questions.answer: It is the ability of the eye lens to change its focal length so that both near and distant objects are seen clearly. The near point of a normal eye is about 25 cm.
keyPoints: Change in focal length of the eye lens
questions.explanation: The ciliary muscles change the curvature of the lens.

questions.topic: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
questions.q: Why do stars twinkle but planets do not?
questions.answer: Starlight is refracted by the changing layers of the atmosphere, and a star is a point source so its apparent position and brightness flicker. A planet is a larger extended source, so the variations average out.
keyPoints: Planets are extended sources so effects average out
questions.explanation: Twinkling is an effect of the atmosphere.

questions.q: The SI unit of electric current is
questions.explanation: Current is measured in amperes.

questions.q: A 12 V battery drives a current of 3 A through a resistor. The resistance is
Resistors of 2 ohm, 3 ohm and 6 ohm are connected in parallel. Their equivalent resistance is
A device used to measure electric current in a circuit is the
questions.explanation: An ammeter is connected in series to measure current.

questions.q: If the length of a wire is doubled while its material and thickness stay the same, its resistance
questions.explanation: Resistance is directly proportional to length.

questions.q: An electric heater of 1000 W is used for 2 hours. The energy consumed is
questions.explanation: Energy = power x time = 1 kW x 2 h = 2 kWh.

questions.q: State Ohm's law.
questions.answer: At constant temperature, the potential difference across the ends of a conductor is directly proportional to the current through it, so V = IR.
questions.explanation: The constant of proportionality is the resistance.

questions.q: Why is tungsten used to make the filament of electric bulbs?
questions.answer: Tungsten has a very high melting point, so it does not melt at the high temperature of a glowing filament, and its high resistivity makes it heat up and glow strongly.
questions.explanation: The filament must stay solid while white hot.

questions.q: Outside a bar magnet, magnetic field lines go from
options: the north pole to the south pole
the south pole to the north pole
questions.explanation: By convention, field lines emerge from the north pole and enter the south pole.

questions.q: A straight conductor carrying an electric current produces
questions.explanation: Oersted showed that a current produces a magnetic field around the wire.

questions.q: In Fleming's left-hand rule, the thumb points in the direction of
options: the force or motion of the conductor
questions.explanation: The forefinger shows the field, the middle finger shows the current and the thumb shows the force.

questions.q: A device that converts electrical energy into mechanical energy is the
questions.explanation: An electric motor uses the force on a current-carrying coil in a magnetic field.

questions.q: When a magnet is moved into a coil connected to a galvanometer the needle deflects. This phenomenon is called
questions.explanation: A changing magnetic field induces a current in the coil.

questions.q: A magnet is held at rest inside a coil connected to a galvanometer and there is no deflection. This is because
options: the magnet has lost its magnetism
there is no change of magnetic field through the coil, so no current is induced
galvanometers work only with alternating current
questions.explanation: Induction needs a changing magnetic field through the coil.

questions.q: Write two properties of magnetic field lines.
questions.answer: Field lines are closed curves that go from the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet. They never cross each other, and a closer spacing of lines shows a stronger field.
keyPoints: Closed curves from north to south outside the magnet
questions.explanation: Field lines are a way to picture the magnetic field.

questions.q: What is the function of a split ring commutator in a DC electric motor?
questions.answer: The split ring commutator reverses the direction of current in the coil after every half rotation. This keeps the force on the coil in the same sense so that it continues to rotate in one direction.
keyPoints: Reverses current direction every half turn
Coil keeps rotating in the same direction
questions.explanation: Without it the coil would just oscillate.

questions.q: Which of the following is a producer in a food chain?
questions.explanation: Green plants make their own food by photosynthesis.

questions.q: The flow of energy in a food chain is
questions.explanation: Energy flows from producers to consumers and is not returned to the Sun.

questions.q: Food chains rarely have more than four or five trophic levels because
options: energy is lost at each level so very little is left for higher levels
questions.explanation: Only about 10 percent of energy passes to the next level.

questions.q: About what percentage of the energy is passed on from one trophic level to the next?
questions.explanation: This is the 10 percent law of energy transfer.

questions.q: Which group of chemicals is mainly responsible for damaging the ozone layer?
questions.explanation: CFCs release chlorine in the stratosphere, which breaks down ozone.

questions.q: A pesticide sprayed on crops is later found in high concentration in hawks that feed on small birds. This is called
questions.explanation: Non-biodegradable chemicals build up in higher trophic levels.

questions.q: What are decomposers? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Decomposers break down dead plants and animals into simple substances that return to the soil. Examples are bacteria and fungi.
questions.explanation: They recycle nutrients.

questions.q: Differentiate between biodegradable and non-biodegradable substances with one example each.
questions.answer: Biodegradable substances such as vegetable peels and paper are broken down by microorganisms. Non-biodegradable substances such as plastics and glass are not, so they remain in the environment for a very long time.
questions.explanation: The difference lies in whether decomposers can break them down.
